subsystems.name: Tube and vacuum envelope
subsystems.role: holds a near-vacuum so aerodynamic drag on the capsule becomes negligible.

subsystems.name: Levitation and guidance
subsystems.role: lifts the capsule clear of the track so nothing wears by contact at high speed.
parts: superconducting or permanent magnets on the capsule
levitation and guidance coils in the track

subsystems.name: Propulsion and power
subsystems.role: pushes the capsule along the tube without an onboard engine.
parts: linear synchronous motor stator in the tube wall

subsystems.name: Capsule
subsystems.role: carries passengers or freight inside a pressure shell.

subsystems.name: Stations and airlocks
subsystems.role: move capsules between atmospheric pressure and vacuum without losing the vacuum.

subsystems.name: Control, safety and evacuation
subsystems.role: keeps a vehicle travelling at aircraft speed safe in a sealed tube.

buildSteps.title: Survey and fix the alignment
buildSteps.detail: The corridor must be exceptionally straight: at 1,000 km/h, comfortable curve radii run to tens of kilometres, so the route is chosen from terrain, geology and land ownership before anything is built.

buildSteps.title: Build foundations and piers
buildSteps.detail: Elevated piers (or a bored tunnel) carry the tube, with settlement monitoring because millimetre movement over kilometres becomes a track problem.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture tube sections
buildSteps.detail: Factory-built steel or concrete pipe sections are shipped to site, lifted onto the piers and joined by welding or bolted flanges, with expansion joints spaced to absorb daily thermal movement.

buildSteps.title: Install the track and stator
buildSteps.detail: Levitation coils and the linear-motor stator are fixed inside the tube and aligned to millimetre tolerance along the whole length.

buildSteps.title: Add vacuum plant
buildSteps.detail: Pump stations every few kilometres, plus isolation valves that let a section be sealed off and vented for maintenance while the rest stays evacuated.

buildSteps.title: Build capsules and airlocks
buildSteps.detail: Capsules are assembled and pressure-tested in a factory; airlock chambers are built at each station so a capsule can be pumped down before entering the tube.

buildSteps.title: Pump down and leak-test
buildSteps.detail: The tube is evacuated in stages to roughly one-thousandth of atmospheric pressure, and leak rates are measured over days; continuous pumping runs for the life of the line.

buildSteps.title: Commission in stages
buildSteps.detail: Low-speed runs first, then increasing vacuum and speed, usually starting with freight before any passenger service.

prerequisites.why: commercial maglev lines already run at up to 430 km/h and test vehicles have gone faster; levitation itself is proven.
linear synchronous and induction motors are in service on maglev lines and can drive a capsule from the track.
particle accelerators hold ultra-high vacuum over tens of kilometres, but through pipes centimetres across — nobody has held it in a tube wide enough for people.

prerequisites.tech: Tube materials and joints that survive thermal cycling
prerequisites.why: hundreds of kilometres of tube expand and contract daily, and every seal and weld is a potential leak that costs pumping power.
a capsule at aircraft speed inside a sealed tube needs fire suppression, pressurisation and escape routes that no test track has yet demonstrated.

pathway.milestone: short test tracks operating at low vacuum, while standard maglev carries passengers daily
pathway.unlocks: proven levitation, propulsion and control, but not yet a sealed vacuum tube.

pathway.milestone: sealed full-vacuum test track a few kilometres long with a working station airlock, demonstrating a capsule above 700 km/h
pathway.unlocks: evidence that vacuum can be held and that a capsule can enter and leave it safely.

pathway.milestone: a first short revenue line, most likely freight in a low-traffic corridor of 10–50 km
pathway.unlocks: real operating data on pumping energy, leaks and maintenance cost.

pathway.milestone: intercity corridors of hundreds of kilometres
pathway.unlocks: the energy-per-passenger advantage over short-haul aviation only if the tube holds vacuum reliably and traffic is dense enough to justify the pumping load.
